open_obligations: Check the appendix sample size and whether the negative result is statistically clear.
Note the different outcome measure (picking the correct solution) from Saunders et al.'s flaw counts.
Check whether scaling critic compute was ever tried, as the authors suggest.
in.other_title: LLM critics did not help humans pick correct solutions to hard contest-code problems
in.rationale: Saunders et al. warn that positive critique results on an easy-to-evaluate task might not reproduce on harder tasks. McAleese et al. report broadly negative results on paired passing and failing solutions to hard competition-style problems: LLM critiques struggled to help contractors pick the correct solution within 20 minutes, which the authors suspect reflects critic compute not being scaled; this is an appendix result without code execution.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether critique assistance still helps humans on tasks that are genuinely hard to evaluate, for contractors judging hard competition-code solutions

open_obligations: Check that inserted bugs are hard to evaluate in the sense Saunders et al. mean, not only time-consuming.
Read together with McAleese et al.'s negative appendix result on hard contest problems.
Note that the contractor cohort is representative of ChatGPT contractors, not best-possible reviewers.
in.other_title: LLM critics preferred over human critiques and catch more human-inserted bugs
in.rationale: Saunders et al. note their task took humans up to about ten minutes, leaving little headroom. McAleese et al. evaluate code where contractors with median 5 years of Python experience spend about 50 minutes per critique and report LLM critics catch many more inserted bugs than the human annotators; the bugs are human-inserted, not natural.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether LLM critiques help on a harder evaluation task than topic-based summarisation, for code review by experienced contractors

text: The authors state their base task is not very hard for humans to evaluate, leaving little headroom for assistance; humans take up to around ten minutes, so little speed-up is observed. They note model-assisted evaluation is most valuable on tasks actually difficult for humans, so positive results on an easier task might not reproduce on harder tasks.
